new_entities.name: Higher maternal choline intake during pregnancy
new_entities.description: Higher dietary intake, circulating status, or supplementation of choline during pregnancy.

new_entities.name: Child cognitive development
new_entities.description: Cognitive, memory, attention, or related neurodevelopmental performance measured during infancy or childhood.

edges.effect_quant: The strongest pattern is inconsistency rather than a single pooled gain. A 2025 systematic review found four prenatal choline trials and five observational cohorts, with most neurodevelopmental outcomes null despite occasional favorable signals.
edges.population: pregnant women and their offspring, including general-population cohorts and smaller supplementation trials
edges.mechanism: Choline donates methyl groups and supports phosphatidylcholine synthesis, acetylcholine production, and fetal membrane formation, so biologic plausibility for neurodevelopment is real. In human studies, however, those mechanistic advantages translate unevenly, suggesting any effect depends on timing, baseline intake, and whether the fetus is under specific stressors such as prenatal alcohol exposure.
edges.summary: This edge should stay conservative. Human pregnancy data support biologic plausibility, and a few trials or cohorts show better infant attention-like outcomes, but most measured cognitive endpoints remain null, so the evidence is mixed rather than convincingly protective.
edges.caveats: The literature mixes supplementation trials, circulating biomarker studies, and special-risk cohorts. Positive findings are often endpoint-specific or seen in subgroups, while broader infant cognition batteries and childhood IQ results are frequently neutral.

evidence.notes: Choline During Pregnancy and Child Neurodevelopment: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials and Observational Studies.
